title: Interface Change Resilience (ICR) framework for tool-call ABI compatibility during rollouts
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build an Interface Change Resilience (ICR) framework that continuously evaluates structured-output and tool-call ABI compatibility during canary, A/B, and shadow rollouts. The ICR framework will compute stability scores from schema validation, function-call diffs, and downstream error signals; surface sample diffs in the Console; and trigger automatic rollback policies when compatibility regressions exceed thresholds. The goal is to reduce silent integration regressions for customers using function-calling and structured outputs during model upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: ICR agent runs in parallel to runtime during canary/AB/shadow and evaluates 100% of shadowed invocations for selected routes
Schema validator supports JSON Schema v7-ish subset used by function-call argument shapes and returns per-invocation pass/fail
Function-call diff detects: added/removed calls, change in call order, changed argument types/keys, changed return shape; outputs a human-readable diff sample
Stability score computed per-model-per-route with configurable thresholds; documented formula and SLOs
Console dashboard shows live stability score, trend, and top sample diffs; links to sampled invocation payloads in object store

Auto-rollback policy implemented that: (a) transitions canary to 'paused' when score < threshold, (b) triggers rollback when sustained degradation over configured window, and (c) creates an incident with recommended rollback change
End-to-end smoke test: deploying a test model with a synthetic breaking change should be auto-rolled back in a controlled CI run
Unit + integration tests cover validator edge cases (nullable fields, optional args, extra unknown keys), and load test proves <5% added p95 latency for monitored routes
Runbook / playbook and security review completed for production enablement
notes: We intentionally keep schema validation permissive by default (warn mode) and opt-in strict enforcement per-route to avoid false positives for early experiments.

Stability score is a weighted function: 40% schema_violation_rate, 30% function_call_parity_gap, 20% downstream_error_delta, 10% user-facing-error_increase. We will iterate weights after initial canaries.
Sampling strategy: full shadow for first 5 minutes of a canary, then 10% uniform sample; all failing invocations are always retained for debugging.
Because structured outputs are customer-coupled, include an opt-out flag for customers who don't want auto-rollback actions (they receive alerts only).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): design API for validators, define scoring, and build a lightweight prober that runs in shadow mode; land design doc and console wireframes
Phase 2 (3 weeks): implement JSON-schema-based validator, function-call diff engine, and sampling/retention plumbing into runtime; expose telemetry metrics
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Console dashboard + alert rules + auto-rollback orchestration with safety checks and manual override
Phase 4 (1 week): runbench load tests, privacy/security review, and staged rollout to internal teams
Phase 5 (ongoing): tune thresholds, add heuristics for noisy fields, and expand supported schema features
risks_and_mitigations: False positives from permissive schemas: provide warn-only mode and per-route strictness controls
Telemetry volume increase from full shadowing: implement retention TTL and batching; initially run full shadow only for short windows
Auto-rollback too aggressive: add probation windows, require sustained degradation over multiple samples, and provide manual approval hooks
Customer trust: add opt-out and email/signal before automated action for enterprise customers
